candidates.computation_change_reason: These column headers define the categories of numeric limits (use-design limits, aquatic/human-health limits, concentration vs. load forms, and daily vs. monthly averaging). A different reading of which column applies to a given discharge point or parameter would change which enforceable numeric limit is selected for compliance comparison.

Every pollutant row in this segment shows N/A in all limit columns. Whether N/A means no enforceable numeric limit exists, limits are not applicable to the relevant use or water body, or numeric values are simply absent from this excerpt would change whether a compliance comparison can be performed (Purpose A) and whether missing or non-comparable results should be classified as no numeric comparison applicable versus unresolved missing-evidence states (Purpose C).

This grouping header separates a class of pollutants from the preceding general pollutant list. Whether monitoring obligations are evaluated per listed compound or by pesticide/PCB class could change which requirements are considered applicable for facilities reporting members of this group.

The phrase bundles DDT with unspecified derivatives. Different interpretations of which compounds count as covered derivatives would change parameter matching for limit selection (Purpose A) and which related monitoring requirements are treated as applicable (Purpose B).

PCBs is listed as a single pollutant entry with one CAS number rather than individual congeners or Aroclor mixtures. Whether reported PCB results map to this aggregate entry or to specific PCB parameters affects which limit and monitoring obligation applies.

This row lacks a STORET code while other pollutants include one. Ambiguity in how to match reported measurements to this parameter (CAS-only vs. STORET-based identification) could change limit applicability, monitoring obligation evaluation, and whether absent or unmatched results remain unresolved.

The spelling 'Epoixde' may be a transcription error for Heptachlor Epoxide. If matched to a different compound name or CAS, the selected limit, monitoring requirement, and classification of missing evidence for related measurements could change.

The CAS formatting '1031-7-8' is non-standard and may represent 1031-07-8 or another identifier. Different normalization or matching rules would change which parameter row applies and therefore limit and monitoring evaluations for reported endosulfan-related results.
